title: fix(lint)!: refuse a hook or job body that does not compile in the (ctx) wrapper the runtime runs it in
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-sales"} -->
_Requested by **Sales** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4Uu?thread=cmsg_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4UuN4HJwYpEVN4miNNeg3Dyvp)_
repo:objectstack#1 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgTggz8AL2bCABoDGis

Fixes #34987

Clause-②: no (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: narrowed
Skills-docs: follow-up #35714 — skills/objectstack-data/references/data-hooks.md (its "Sandbox restrictions" section teaches what a hook body may contain and names no compile check; not a `domain:skills` PR, so `skills/**` is not edited here)

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:hook 与 job 的 L2 脚本体(`body.language: 'js'`)现在在运行时真正包裹它们的 `(async (ctx) => { … })` 里做一次编译检查;编译不过的报 `hook-body-does-not-compile` / `job-body-does-not-compile`,级别 error,`os validate` / `os build` / `os lint` 与 hook 的发布门都会拒收。
- 为什么改:此前这类脚本体(如 `const ctx = ctx.input || {}`、同名 `let` 声明两次)能通过所有作者期检查,部署后每次运行都在第一条语句前抛 SyntaxError;action 已有同款检查(action-body-does-not-compile),hook 和 job 没有。
- 风险与回滚:只拒收本来就永远跑不起来的脚本体;示例应用、技能、文档样例实测零命中。运行时的 hook/job 包裹改为从同一个函数生成,字节与原先完全一致。回滚 = revert 本 PR。
- 先看:`packages/lint/src/validate-hook-body-compiles.ts`(新规则本体);`packages/runtime/src/sandbox/quickjs-runner.ts` 中 `hookBodyFunctionExpression(args.source)` 那一处 hunk(运行时包裹来源);`packages/lint/src/validate-action-body-compiles.ts` 中抽出的 `judgeBodyCompile`(action 规则输出须保持不变)。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/validate-hook-body-compiles.test.ts`,预期 11 个用例全绿,其中一个不可编译的 hook 与一个不可编译的 job 各报 error。
- 需要你做的:无,席位落地。

## What changes

- **One spelling of the `(ctx)` wrapper.** `hookBodyFunctionExpression(source)` and `HOOK_BODY_PARAMETERS` join `actionBodyFunctionExpression` in `packages/lint/src/action-body-wrapper.ts` (exported from `@objectstack/lint`, the function also from `@objectstack/lint/runtime`). `quickjs-runner.ts` now builds the hook and job wrapper from it instead of spelling it inline; the produced text is byte-identical to what it built before. Measured in the runner: hooks and jobs both take `(async (ctx) => { SOURCE })(globalThis.__ctx)` (the runner's only branch is `origin.kind !== 'action'`), so there is one wrapper for both, not two.
- **The compile core is shared.** `judgeBodyCompile(expression, parameters)` (with `bodyCompileMessage` / `bodyCompileHint`) is lifted out of `validateActionBodyCompiles` unchanged in behaviour: the regular-expression pattern/token split from the previous change is reused as is, not altered. `action-body-does-not-compile`'s findings are byte-identical (its 25 pins pass unedited).
- **New gating rule `validateHookAndJobBodyCompiles`**, rule ids `hook-body-does-not-compile` and `job-body-does-not-compile` (decision: two new ids rather than widening the action id, because the id names the body kind and `os explain` / `suppressWarnings` address one kind; one walk and one registry entry, because the wrapper is one). Same severity split as the action rule. Walks `hooks[*].body` and `jobs[*].body`, `language: 'js'` only; a hook lowered from an inline `handler` is located at `hooks[N].handler`.
- **Doors.** All three CLI commands; runtime publish gate `runtimeTypes: ['hook']`. A job is `allowRuntimeCreate: false`, so no door publishes one, and `hooks` is not an ObjectSchema key, so no object write carries a hook. The rule loads no dependency (host `node:vm`), so it is safe on the kernel boot path.
- `os explain` pages for both ids; `hook-bodies.mdx` gains the check; `validating-metadata.mdx` gains its door-table row; the four CLI transcripts that print the author-time rule count read 74 (a direct consequence of the new registry entry, caught by `check:docs-transcript-drift`).
- ADR-0087 semantic entry `hook-job-body-does-not-compile-refused`; the action entry's sentence "hook and job bodies are not judged" is corrected to point at it. ADR-0077 Decision 3 (a hook body always requires human review) is untouched: this adds a build error and lowers no review friction.

## Tests

- `packages/lint/src/validate-hook-body-compiles.test.ts` (11 cases): one uncompilable hook (`const ctx = ctx.input || {}; return 1;` → `hook-body-does-not-compile`, `error`, `hooks[0].body.source`) and one uncompilable job (`let x = 1; let x = 2;` → `job-body-does-not-compile`, `error`, `jobs[0].body.source`); the parse check reporting nothing on both; the severity split (pattern warns, token refused); controls that valid bodies, L1 bodies and handler-only hooks pass; lowered-hook location; never-runs; `os explain`; the door tests over `os validate` / `os build` / `os lint` and the runtime publish gate (refused and admitted).

## Acceptance notes

- First-party exposure, measured: 0. Static scan of `{ language: 'js', source }` literals across `examples/**`, `apps/**`, `skills/**`, `content/docs/**` (releases excluded) and `packages/qa/**`: 33 literal bodies judged, 22 built from variables or interpolations (all in dogfood tests, which the dogfood battery runs), 0 refused. One docs fence in `hook-bodies.mdx` (the compiled-artifact shape) elides its body with an ellipsis; it is prose, not metadata. Compiled artifacts: `app-crm` 1 hook body and `app-showcase` 8 hook bodies (its one job carries a `handler`, no body), 0 refused; `os validate` over all four examples exits 0 with no finding of either id.
- L1 expression hook bodies run in a different wrapper (`(function(){ return (SOURCE); })()`) and are outside this rule.
- At run time a hook or job body that still fails to compile answers the runner's generic `hook 'NAME' threw: SyntaxError …`, not the coded sentence actions get (`actionBodyCompileFailure`). Noted, not filed: the author-time refusal now covers the doors, and the run-time sentence already names the body and the error.
- Duplicate Fix Guard: this PR's branch is `claude/project-thread-iswnar`, not `claude/issue-34987-*`. Platform exception: this card thread can push only its assigned branch; the claim (comment 7025754901) names it.

## Verification

All readings on head `ed1bf2038` (merge of `origin/main` 238661f47 into the branch), unless a line names another.

<details><summary>Unit and package suites</summary>

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint test` → Test Files 222 passed (222), Tests 9336 passed (9336); `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint typecheck` and `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime typecheck` exit 0 (`VERDICT command-exit 0`).
- Pre-merge head `e1209577f`: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test` → 861 files / 27494 passed; `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime test` → 631 files / 11629 passed, 25 skipped (`VERDICT command-exit 0`). The merge brought no runtime or spec change.

</details>

<details><summary>Door probe (os validate) and first-party exposure</summary>

- A probe stack with the uncompilable hook and the uncompilable job: `os validate` exits 1 and prints `hook "stamp_owner" › body: body does not compile in the wrapper the runtime runs it in, (async (ctx) => { … }) (SyntaxError: Identifier 'ctx' has already been declared, line 1), so every run of this hook fails` at `hooks[0].body.source`, and the same for `job "nightly_close"` at `jobs[0].body.source`.
- `os validate --json` over `app-todo`, `app-crm`, `app-showcase`, `app-multi-package`: exit 0 each, 0 findings of either id. Static scan after the merge: 33 literal bodies judged, 0 refused (one ellipsis docs fence, prose).

</details>

<details><summary>Ablation (one, committed first)</summary>

`node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` on `validate-hook-body-compiles.ts`, anchor `recordsOf(stack.hooks).forEach` replaced by `recordsOf(undefined).forEach`: anchor 1 to 0, blob 7abe508df968 to 8271a15f3259; the card's test file went red as predicted, 5 failed / 6 passed of 11 (every hook pin red, the job pin green). Restore proven: blob equals HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty. The subject resolves through relative `src/` imports, so no `dist/` leg applies.

</details>

<details><summary>Gates</summary>

- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --commands` at `ed1bf2038`: 118 commands, all run, all `exit 0`; `--ran` reconciliation: `118 derived, 118 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN` (a derived zero, every line carries its exit code).
- `check:docs-transcript-drift` was red on the first sweep (the new registry entry moves the printed author-time rule count from 73 to 74); fixed in `e1209577f`, green since.
- Local-only `check:dev-prereqs`: exit 1, 35 unbuilt `ui/` workspace dists. A fact about this container, not this diff, which touches no `ui/` path.

</details>

<details><summary>Dogfood battery (narrowing arm, once on the final head)</summary>

`ed1bf20389b9d8f1d4126e2265ffdf7c55fde1d9`: closure build, then `pnpm --filter @objectstack/dogfood test` under the verify lock. `VERDICT command-exit 0`, Test Files 482 passed, 3 skipped (485), Tests 4093 passed, 68 skipped (4161), no failure.

</details>
